title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Environment Readiness (Acme Medical Systems)
transcript:
[00:00] Emily (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick POC weekly sync, hope this time works. We have Ravi from the SE team and Maya from CSM.
[00:22] John (CTO): Yup works. we got a couple people pulled in. we'll go over onboarding, access, and the environment readiness stuff.
[00:35] Emily (AE): Great. quick agenda: one, access status and network; two, pilot results and perf numbers you ran; three, tuning recommendations; four, open blockers and next steps.
[00:47] Priya (ML Eng): sounds good. we pushed the test harness last night, ran a small batch of inference on the hosted trial.
[00:56] Ravi (SE): Awesome. before we jump numbers, access — Daniel, are you still blocked on VPC peering and the firewall rules? last I saw the ticket was in progress.
[01:10] Daniel (DevOps): we're 90% there. firewall needed a few ports opened for the Redwood dedicated agents: 443 outbound plus a pair of ephemeral ports for health checks. we had to loop in network. Also we needed to whitelist the subnets for the egress.
[01:27] Ravi (SE): Cool. for VPC peering note, make sure routes are pushed both ways and Nat gateway allows the peered traffic. we can re-send the exact CIDR list.
[01:37] Daniel: please yes, resend. I think we missed the secondary range.
[01:41] Emily (AE): I'll drop the CIDR list in the notes and re-share the runbook link.
[01:47] Maya (CSM): I'll follow up on the ticket and make sure it's escalated if it slips beyond tomorrow.
[01:55] Sara (Security): on the security side we still need SAML assertions for SSO and confirmation on HKMS/KMS integration. you mentioned a customer-managed KMS option last week?
[02:06] Ravi (SE): Yep. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS; for the private deployment we also offer HSM integration. For the hosted trial we can simulate KMS but for pilot you'll want to supply a key alias.
[02:19] Sarah (sic) Sara (Security): okay, simulate is fine for now, but we will need real KMS for any PHI tests.
[02:27] Emily (AE): noted. we'll put the KMS integration checklist on the share.
[02:33] Ben (PM): quick question on data residency — our legal team wants logs retained in us-east only. can you enforce region routing?
[02:42] Ravi (SE): Yes, routing policy can pin requests to region. For the POC we've been using hosted-us-east. We can confirm log storage is in us-east; I'll pull the policy doc and share.
[02:53] Priya (ML Eng): moving to perf results — we ran two models: redwood/fast-7b quantized and an open-7b baseline. End-to-end latency medians: 220ms for redwood fast 7b and ~350ms for open baseline on our test prompts, batch size 1. Token cost estimate looked like $0.0009/token for fast-7b vs $0.0014 for baseline — rough numbers.
[03:23] Ravi (SE): Those numbers sound in line with expectations. What prompt lengths and seq lengths were you using?
[03:30] Priya: prompts avg 120 tokens, generation avg 80 tokens. We used default beamless sampling.
[03:36] Ravi: Good. For latency tuning you can enable continuous batching and increase max_batch_latency to 15ms if you can tolerate a few ms more; that improves amortized GPU utilization.
[03:46] Priya: we tried batching to 4 and saw latency jump to ~280ms but tokens/sec improved.
[03:52] Emily: that's the typical tradeoff — cost vs median latency. we'll add recommended batch configs per workload.
[03:59] John: any regressions on quality when using quantized models? we have one test suite of 50 prompts that we run for clinical-sounding outputs.
[04:08] Priya: minimal. we saw a slight hallucination increase on a couple prompts for the 4-bit quant, but acceptable so far.
[04:16] Ravi: We can recommend fallback policies to a higher-precision variant for flagged prompts, or run a quality check route that uses the non-quant model for high-risk types.
[04:27] Ben: cost math — can you give a ballpark monthly cost if we scale to 200k requests/day?
[04:34] Emily: rough ballpark depends on tokens per request, but at 200k short prompts (200 tokens total), throughput optimized with batching you'd see a significant reduction vs naive per-request. We can run a spreadsheet. I'll attach a cost model.
[04:47] Priya: we actually started a small suite of benchmark csvs — link: https://acme.share/benchmarks/poc_week1.csv (internal).
[04:56] Ravi: good, we'll ingest that and run the recommended profile.
[05:00] John: any platform issues in the logs? we had one error where the session dropped and the client retried 3 times.
[05:08] Maya (CSM): I saw the alert; looks like a transient backend reconnect. Ravi, you want to comment?
[05:13] Ravi: there was a brief node restart during autoscaling — lasted ~30s. Our runtime has auto-retry and fallback to a warm standby but in some cases clients will see a few retried requests. we've fixed the autoscale policy in the trial cluster.
[05:26] Priya: can you share the tracing info for that window?
[05:29] Ravi: yes I'll share the trace ids and a small write-up.
[05:33] Sara (Security): also we need audit log format for SIEM ingestion. Does Redwood emit logs with RFC 5424 fields?
[05:42] Ravi: We emit structured JSON logs and can forward to your SIEM via Kinesis/Events. For POC we can provide a sample log export.
[05:50] Daniel: about the private deployment option — if we go private later, how disruptive is switching?
[05:56] Emily: it's non-trivial but we've done multiple migrations. The API surface stays the same; config and network work are the main effort. We'll prepare a migration plan and estimate 4-6 weeks for a full private rollout depending on infra.
[06:09] Ben: timeline — we are targeting a pilot conclusion and decision by end of March. is that feasible?
[06:15] Emily: yes if onboarding finishes this week and the perf pass happens next week we can meet that timeline.
[06:22] John: what's left to call onboarding finished? list it out please.
[06:26] Maya (CSM): items: VPC peering completed, SSO configured, KMS key provided (or test simulate), test harness passing 2 smoke suites, and baseline benchmark uploaded.
[06:39] Daniel: I think VPC and firewall are the only infra blockers. SSO we have a SAML provider ready; we need the service provider metadata from Redwood.
[06:48] Emily: I'll send the SP metadata after the call.
[06:51] Priya: on tuning, you recommended KV cache for repeated context. we tried enabling prefix cache and saw a 20% token compute reduction on a long-conversation test.
[06:59] Ravi: great. for chat-heavy workflows prefix/KV cache is the biggest wins. also for reranking use-case, try using embeddings for candidate prefiltering to save tokens.
[07:12] Priya: noted. we have a rerank flow; will experiment.
[07:16] John: any legal/procurement notes — we are pulling our legal team in next Wed. can you share SOC2 and ISO docs?
[07:24] Emily: yes we have the SOC 2 template and ISO attestation; I'll share redacted copies — link: https://redwood.ai/compliance (redacted link).
[07:33] Sara: also need the DPA draft.
[07:36] Emily: will send DPA draft and the onboarding checklist.
[07:39] Ben: small UX ask — latency spikes at tail can affect the product. can Redwood provide p95 and p99 metrics in the console?
[07:46] Ravi: yes we have p50/p95/p99 per route and token-level breakdown in the console; we'll enable a dashboard for your account.
[07:55] Priya: when will we get the tuned model config and quantization recommendation?
[07:59] Ravi: I'll produce a short config bundle (batching, kv settings, quant profile) and share by Thursday.
[08:06] Emily: good. let's recap blockers and next steps.
[08:09] Maya (CSM): recap: Daniel to finish VPC/firewall, Redwood to send SP metadata and CIDR list, Ravi to share traces and config bundle, Emily to send compliance docs and cost spreadsheet, Priya to upload full benchmark csv.
[08:26] John: timeline check again — next sync same time next week?
[08:30] Emily: yes same time next week.
[08:33] Ben: small note: we might want a mid-week ad-hoc once VPC is done.
[08:37] Emily: fine. we'll be available.
[08:40] John: thanks everyone.
[08:42] Emily: thanks — we'll follow up with notes, action items, and links.
[08:46] (call ends)
next_steps: Redwood to send CIDR list and SP metadata
Ravi to share trace ids and tuning config by Thursday
Emily to send SOC2/ISO/DPA redacted docs and cost spreadsheet
Daniel to complete VPC peering and update ticket
Priya to upload full benchmark csv to shared folder
action_items: Daniel Ruiz | Complete VPC peering and firewall rules | 2025-02-15
Ravi Patel | Share trace ids and tuning/config bundle | 2025-02-20
Emily Zhao | Share compliance docs, CIDR list, SP metadata, and cost spreadsheet | 2025-02-17
Priya Menon | Upload full benchmark CSV and test results | 2025-02-16
